issues.title: Wrong sign in the degree-7 Padé endpoint condition

failure_location.quote: For instance, the update rule of the third method in this family is defined by $p(x) = \frac1{16}\left(35x - 35x^3 + 21x^5 - 5x^7\right)$, which is the unique degree-7 polynomial satisfying $p(\pm 1) = 1$ and $p'(\pm1) = p''(\pm 1) = p'''(\pm 1) = 0$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For instance, the update rule of the third method in this family is defined by $p(x) = \frac1{16}\left(35x - 35x^3 + 21x^5 - 5x^7\right)$, which is the unique degree-7 polynomial satisfying $p(\pm 1) = 1$ and $p'(\pm1) = p''(\pm 1) = p'''(\pm 1) = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the displayed polynomial takes the value +1 at both endpoints. The displayed formula is odd and evaluates to p(1)=1, so it necessarily has p(-1)=-1. Thus the formula supports p(±1)=±1, not the old assertion.
issues.overall_effect: The stated Hermite/Padé characterization of the displayed degree-7 update is false at the negative endpoint, although no later formal result depends on the erroneous sign.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the endpoint condition p(±1)=1 by p(±1)=±1, leaving the derivative conditions and uniqueness characterization unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The displayed polynomial is visibly odd and evaluates to 1 at x=1, so the old source uniquely forces p(-1)=-1. This is an isolated sign transcription with no dependent argument or result to repair.

issues.title: Wrong sign in the inverse-Newton endpoint condition

failure_location.quote: Observing that $r(x) = \frac{2x}{1+x^2}$ satisfies $r(\pm 1) = 1$ and $r'(\pm 1) = 0$, we see that (inverse) Newton is also a Padé method, though a rational rather than polynomial one.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Observing that $r(x) = \frac{2x}{1+x^2}$ satisfies $r(\pm 1) = 1$ and $r'(\pm 1) = 0$, we see that (inverse) Newton is also a Padé method, though a rational rather than polynomial one.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the inverse-Newton rational function equals +1 at both endpoints. Its displayed formula instead gives r(1)=1 and r(-1)=-1. The correct interpolation condition is therefore r(±1)=±1; the derivative assertion remains unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The stated reason that inverse Newton matches the sign function as a rational Padé method is false at the negative endpoint as written, but no formal result depends on that sign error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace r(±1)=1 by r(±1)=±1, retaining r'(±1)=0 and the Padé-method conclusion.
issues.why_classification: The displayed rational function is visibly odd and directly gives r(1)=1 and r(-1)=-1. The correction is uniquely forced by the old source and requires no repair to any downstream argument.

issues.title: Quintic coefficient discarded in the Remez refinement

failure_location.quote: Once we have solved for $a_1,b_1,c_1,$ and $E_1$ we set $p^{(k)}(x) = a_1x+b_1x^3 + b_1x^5$.

issues.failure_explanation: The old refinement instructs the reader to use b_1 for both the cubic and quintic terms after solving for a separate c_1. Equation eq:linearsystem instead establishes c as the coefficient of x^5, so the constructed polynomial and its stated stationary-point equation do not implement the preceding solve.
issues.overall_effect: The prose-specified Remez refinement would compute extrema for a polynomial different from the one produced by its linear system. The minimax theory itself and the separately displayed intended coefficient roles are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the separately solved quintic coefficient throughout: set p^(k)(x)=a_k x+b_k x^3+c_k x^5 and compute its stationary points from a_k+3b_k x^2+5c_k x^4=0. The linear solve and the rest of the Remez procedure can remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The linear system clearly assigns c_k to x^5, but the erroneous b_k is propagated into the stationary-point equation, so the literal refinement construction relies on the wrong polynomial and is not merely an isolated glyph error. Two routine, source-supported substitutions restore the intended algorithm without a new lemma or any loss of guarantee.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: a degree-5 odd polynomial $p_k(x) = a_k x + b_k x^3 + c_k x^5$

issues.title: Remez input contract permits a singular initial system
issues.failure_explanation: For any nondegenerate positive interval away from the early-return branch, the old input contract permits choosing $x_1^{(1)}=u$. In eq:linearsystem this makes the row $[x_1^{(1)},(x_1^{(1)})^3,(x_1^{(1)})^5,-1]$ identical to the final u-row, so the displayed inverse is undefined. Similarly, $x_2^{(1)}=\ell$ duplicates the first row.
issues.overall_effect: A caller satisfying the stated input contract can encounter a singular first Remez solve and receive no polynomial; the higher-level offline construction also lacks a safe initial-point interface.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Whenever the linear-solve branch is reached with ℓ<u, choose the initial points internally as x_1^(1)=(3ℓ+u)/4 and x_2^(1)=(ℓ+3u)/4, rather than accepting unrestricted points in [ℓ,u]. Use this same safe initialization in the higher-level offline call.
issues.why_classification: The old input contract genuinely admits duplicate rows, so a missing nondegeneracy condition or safe initialization must be supplied. Fixed strictly interior trial points are a short, routine repair already supported by the old Remez discussion; they preserve the interval class, output, and minimax guarantee without nontrivial new work.

issues.title: Incorrect base polynomial in the fast-iteration invariant
issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm initializes $\bm Q_0=\bm I$ and represents the quotient of the composed odd polynomial by x. At iteration zero the empty composition is x, so that quotient is 1. Using q_0(x)=x would instead make the recurrence produce $q_1(x)=x h_1(x^4)$ rather than the required $h_1(x^2)$, invalidating the stated induction.
issues.overall_effect: The executable matrix recurrence is unchanged, but its written base invariant and correctness induction are inconsistent with the initialization and do not establish the advertised output as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the scalar base definition to q_0(x)=1. Then the empty composition is x=xq_0(x), Q_0=I is the correct matrix base case, and the stated recurrence and executable algorithm need no further change.
issues.why_classification: The false value q_0(x)=x is used as the base of the correctness induction, so the proof relies on the erroneous meaning and the defect is substantive rather than a typo under the strict test. The uniquely determined one-line base-case correction restores the same algorithm and output with no mathematical loss.

issues.title: Offline quintic code hard-codes the upper endpoint
issues.failure_explanation: The code claims to implement optimal_quintic(l,u) for inputs satisfying 0≤l≤u, while its initialization uses 1 instead of u. Consequently, for admissible intervals with u<1, a trial point can lie outside [l,u], violating the Remez construction that the helper is said to implement.
issues.overall_effect: The generic offline routine does not implement its stated interval-dependent initialization and can start the Remez solve from inadmissible points, although the special case u=1 masks the error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the two hard-coded upper endpoints by the parameter u: use q=(3*l+u)/4 and r=(l+3*u)/4. No other code or contract needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The generic function signature and the old Remez description already state the interval-dependent quarter-point formulas, uniquely forcing both occurrences of 1 to be u. This is a direct transcriptional correction of the implementation expression; it preserves the advertised generic contract and leaves the u=1 case unchanged.
